results.reason: Issue 1 cites §2.2's 270/240-day window and five-year renewal, and computes the window as Oct 3 to Nov 2, 2026 against the June 30, 2027 expiry. It explains that missing it locks Halvorsen into exclusivity, the non-compete and purchase minimums for five more years. It recommends a signed extension or a protective non-renewal notice before the deadline.

Issue 2A cites §5.3's 30-day objection right and deemed acceptance, receipt on Aug 21, 2026, and a deadline of Sept 20, 2026. It says the objection right has probably lapsed and recommends confirming with the client whether a timely objection was sent, otherwise negotiating commercially.

Issue 5 explains that §11.1 has no fault limiter and could cover claims caused by Brightmere, such as design defects. It notes the indemnity is uncapped under §12.3(a) while Brightmere's §11.2 indemnity is capped. It recommends narrowing §11.1 to Halvorsen's fault and making the cap treatment reciprocal.

Issue 4 explains that Amendment §3.1 replaced §12.3 and removed the §12.3(b) recall carve-out. It says §9.3 recall reimbursement is now subject to the 12-month fees cap, which a large recall could exceed, and recommends restoring §12.3(b).

Issue 3 identifies Amendment §6's Delaware law and Wilmington forum, contrasts them with Agr. §17's New York law and New York County courts, and notes the amendment likely prevails under §1.4. It recommends restoring New York law and courts.
The memo states the Notice was delivered by FedEx on Aug 21, 2026.
The memo states the Initial Term ends June 30, 2027.
The memo states 'Agr. §1.4 ranks amendments first'.
The memo is addressed to the Partner. Each issue gives the document and section under 'Where', explains the impact under 'Why it matters', and sets out a recommended fix.
The memo concludes that recall reimbursement is now capped.
The memo expressly acknowledges that the Delaware provisions now govern.
